headline: Applied Human Science College students block Dhaka road over principal's removal
summary: Students allege police baton-charged them during a midnight rescue operation to free the principal, who had been confined by protesters.
details: Students of the Government College of Applied Human Science in Dhaka have blocked Azimpur Road, demanding the removal of Principal Prof Meherun Nessa.
The protests began after students confined the principal to her office on Thursday, leading to a midnight rescue operation by police.
Students claim that police baton-charged them during the rescue, leaving several students seriously injured and hospitalized.
Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohammad Mostak Sarker denied the allegations, stating that only female officers were deployed to rescue the principal safely.
The dispute reportedly stems from the principal cancelling the residential seats of two students and demanding Tk 12,500 for the use of the college auditorium.
Prof Meherun Nessa denied the allegations, stating that students were punished for using the auditorium from 10am until 5am and were required to pay for electricity bills.
Students have announced an indefinite suspension of all campus activities until the principal resigns and action is taken against the officers involved.
caption:
Students block Azimpur Road in Dhaka after alleging police baton-charged them during a midnight rescue of their principal.

Students of the Government College of Applied Human Science in Dhaka have blocked Azimpur Road, demanding the removal of Principal Prof Meherun Nessa.

The protests began after students confined the principal to her office on Thursday, leading to a midnight rescue operation by police.

Students claim that police baton-charged them during the rescue, leaving several students seriously injured and hospitalized.

Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohammad Mostak Sarker denied the allegations, stating that only female officers were deployed to rescue the principal safely.

The dispute reportedly stems from the principal cancelling the residential seats of two students and demanding Tk 12,500 for the use of the college auditorium.

Prof Meherun Nessa denied the allegations, stating that students were punished for using the auditorium from 10am until 5am and were required to pay for electricity bills.

Students have announced an indefinite suspension of all campus activities until the principal resigns and action is taken against the officers involved.

headline_marked: 2 DGFI members [[dismissed and jailed for a year]] in extortion case
headline: 2 DGFI members dismissed and jailed for a year in extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were convicted following a court martial after attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were involved in an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur on October 25.
The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted by four individuals.
The businessman handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He later managed to alert a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.
Following their arrest by the Mohammadpur Police Station, the two intelligence personnel were handed over to the army for trial under military law.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been dismissed and sentenced to one year in prison after attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were involved in an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur on October 25.

The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted by four individuals.

The businessman handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He later managed to alert a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.

Following their arrest by the Mohammadpur Police Station, the two intelligence personnel were handed over to the army for trial under military law.
